# JCN Space Agent

> Justyn Clark Network browser-first AI workspace runtime for spaces, tools, widgets, music workflows, and local project operations.

## Summary

JCN Space Agent is the JCN-owned Space Agent source tree. It keeps the browser-first runtime architecture while making the source, package metadata, and public documentation fit Justyn Clark's local tool ecosystem instead of the original upstream distribution.

The browser app is the primary runtime. The Node.js side exists as narrow infrastructure around it: page shells, authentication, app-file APIs, module delivery, outbound fetch proxying, local development support, and optional desktop hosting.

This repo is intended to become a personal and extensible operating surface for the JCN project ecosystem, including project awareness, browser-first agent tools, widgets, local model experimentation, Web Audio and MIDI workflows, REAPER-adjacent control surfaces, and recoverable user or group customware.

## What Makes It Different

- The agent can reshape the interface instead of staying trapped inside a fixed product surface.
- Spaces and widgets are first-class browser runtime surfaces.
- The runtime is modular and layered, so capabilities can be added, removed, or swapped without welding everything into one rigid app.
- New capabilities can live in simple `SKILL.md` files, which keeps extension work text-first and agent-friendly.
- The system supports personal use as well as hierarchical group use, with per-user workspaces and shared group layers.
- Admin mode and Git-backed time travel provide a stable recovery path when user or group changes need inspection or rollback.

## Runtime Model

- Browser app first: the browser runtime is the main application.
- Thin server: the Node.js server handles infrastructure concerns rather than becoming the product runtime.
- Layered customware: firmware lives in `app/L0`, group customware in `app/L1`, and user customware in `app/L2`.
- Admin isolation: the `/admin` surface stays firmware-backed even when writable layers exist.
- Documentation-first development: the repository uses a hierarchical `AGENTS.md` contract system so agents can understand ownership, architecture, and local implementation rules before changing code.

## Fast Local Launch

Use this path when you just want the app running locally without creating users or passwords:

```bash
npm install --omit=optional
npm run dev -- PORT=0 CUSTOMWARE_PATH="$HOME/.jcn/space-agent/customware" SINGLE_USER_APP=true
```

Open the printed `space server listening at ...` URL. `PORT=0` asks the OS for a free port, `CUSTOMWARE_PATH` keeps writable user and group state outside the source checkout, and `SINGLE_USER_APP=true` signs the browser in as the local `user` account.

## Login-Based Local Launch

Use this path when you want named users and the normal login shell:

```bash
npm install --omit=optional
node space set CUSTOMWARE_PATH="$HOME/.jcn/space-agent/customware"
node space user create justyn --password "change-me-now" --full-name "Justyn Clark" --groups _admin
node space serve
```

Then open the printed local URL and sign in as `justyn`.

## Key Commands

- `npm run dev`: run the local development supervisor with auto-reload.
- `node space serve`: run the server directly.
- `node space supervise`: run the zero-downtime supervisor for source checkouts.
- `node space get` and `node space set`: inspect or store runtime parameters.
- `node space user create`: create a user such as an initial admin.
- `node space help`: list command families and built-in help.

## Validation

There is not currently one substantive all-in-one `npm test`, `npm run lint`, or `npm run format` suite. Use the smallest relevant checks for the area that changed.

Good baseline checks:

```bash
git diff --check
node tests/yaml_lite_test.mjs
node --test tests/spaces_prompt_context_test.mjs tests/spaces_widget_import_test.mjs
```

For app startup validation:

```bash
npm run dev -- PORT=0 CUSTOMWARE_PATH="$(mktemp -d)" SINGLE_USER_APP=true
```

## Documentation And Agent Development

This repository keeps a documentation hierarchy rooted in `AGENTS.md`, with deeper `AGENTS.md` files for app, server, commands, packaging, tests, and important subsystems. These files are binding runtime and architecture contracts for agents, not optional notes.

The project also uses plain-text `SKILL.md` files for agent capabilities and focused workflows. This keeps much of the extension surface readable and writable by both humans and agents without inventing heavyweight custom formats.
